all_of: a custom error page renders the user-controllable path segment through str() into a Jinja2 template
any payload URL path accepts the full {{ }} namespace without an escaping filter
any_of: a renderer config or lipsum.__globals__ reaches os

chain.action: send GET /{{7*7}} to test whether the custom 404 page renders the path through Jinja2
chain.why: the template calls str() on the input path inside an error output, so the {{ }} namespace is live

chain.action: reach a privileged namespace through lipsum.__globals__.os and confirm with `id` in popen
chain.why: lipsum.__globals__ reaches the app module namespace where os is already imported — no import needed

chain.action: use slash-free shell commands (`ls`, `pwd`, `cat flag.txt`) because the URL route pattern <str> rejects unencoded slashes, reading one command per request
chain.why: raw / in the payload breaks the path match and hits the plain Werkzeug 404 instead of the injectable template

chain.action: popen('cat flag.txt') with the working directory at /, read the flag out of the str() error template
chain.why: the flag lives at filesystem root in the same container

first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the raw payload is escaped or filtered, or the page shows a different 404

blast_radius: arbitrary python execution as root inside the single-container app

verification.evidence: popen cat flag.txt returned the flagged string inside the custom str() call output
verification.proof: GET / with a lipsum-based popen payload returned the flagged string inside the custom error template

reuse_when: an error page names or echoes the input URL through a template that renders it
Flask/Jinja2 renders a path or a config-owned parameter unescaped
a string-conversion error template avoids a dedicated sandbox
known_traps: a slash in the payload breaks the route pattern (<str> does not match slashes); slash-free shell commands are the easy route
